tutorSurveys: Jonah and Christopher were easily distracted today and it distracted the entire group and session. We were not able to get through the lesson. We will continue to work with them to adjust this behavior and I will let Mr.Sabani know as well.

Reminder: This 3D session took place today from 12:35–1:17 p.m. but appears in Pearl at 4:00 p.m.

The 3D and 3B sessions had disappeared from my Pearl schedule. Administrators had previously notified me of the issue, and based on our correspondence, I was under the impression it had been taken care of. When I noticed today that both sessions were still missing, I followed up with the administrators.

Dr. Clemons authorized me to enter an alternate time for the 3D session so I could use the booking feature and said she would add a note in Pearl. She also advised that there was no need to enter the 3B session because the scholars were testing.

Scholars built, read, and spelled long-vowel words using letter manipulatives. They identified the vowel pattern in each word and then applied their reading skills while beginning What If You Had Animal Ears?
i fund something that my scholars are interested in and i will be basing my lessons on it as evidenced by my submitted lesson plans. :)

During today’s session, Christopher successfully demonstrated improved focus and active participation after being seated separately from Jonah. Conversely, Jonah initially resisted the seating adjustment, remained easily distracted, and disrupted his peers; additionally, when given to opportunity to use the restroom he took his time which further reduced his available learning time. While the majority of the students were eager to learn and ready to participate, individual behavioral distractions and extended transitions ultimately reduced the overall instructional time for the group.
The session saw full engagement, with students actively participating and eagerly asking questions to deepen their math understanding.

On wednesday we will continue using base ten blocks and start working on addition math problems as well as regrouping. Scholars shared they were unsure about their regrouping skills. We will focus on that topic next session.
The group is energetic and can be rowdy from time to time but they have fun learning.
Some students are a bit shy but overall they did very well and participated in today's session.
Wonderful group of 3rd graders, all the girls were focused and on task.
They had a lot of energy because they came from recess. But they enjoyed tutoring.
Everyone was wonderful, well behaved and enthusiastic during our session.
